title: Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards Billing Error Training Questions: Accrual Days on a Duplicate Foreign Posting
content:
**What are the accrual days?** For a notice that a purchase processed in a foreign currency or outside the United States posted twice to a Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards account, the accrual days follow the latest statement and the posting in error's own posting date. When the latest statement charged purchase interest and the posting in error posted on or before the latest statement date, they are the calendar days from the latest statement date to the notice date. When the latest statement charged purchase interest and the posting in error posted after the latest statement date, they are the calendar days from its posting date to the notice date. When the latest statement charged no purchase interest, so that the grace period holds, they are zero.

**Does a minimum interest charge on the latest statement count as purchase interest here?** No. Only purchase interest charged on the latest statement counts.

**What is the notice date?** The date the notice is received.

## Worked cases (hypothetical: latest statement dated 30 June, notice received 10 July)

| Latest statement charged | Posting in error posted | Accrual days |
|---|---|---|
| purchase interest | 18 June | from 30 June to 10 July: 10 |
| purchase interest | 4 July | from 4 July to 10 July: 6 |
| only a minimum interest charge | any | 0 |
| no interest | any | 0 |
